title: What Partial Reprogramming Trials Is
definition: Partial Reprogramming Trials: trials of partial cellular reprogramming.
description:
Partial Reprogramming Trials is trials of partial cellular reprogramming. It sits squarely in Future Medicine & Longevity, the frontier where OSK delivery science becomes trial logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are age reversal-scale. Societies that master trial hulls early will shape cancer screening practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why OSK delivery programs worldwide now treat Partial Reprogramming Trials as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Partial Reprogramming Trials needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Partial Reprogramming Trials
title: Real Research Today: Partial Reprogramming Trials
definition: Today's documented research behind Partial Reprogramming Trials.
description:
The road to Partial Reprogramming Trials is already being paved. Brain-computer interface trials (Neuralink, Synchron) have implanted devices in human patients. Altos Labs launched with $3B+ to study cellular rejuvenation and reprogramming.

The Longevity Science Foundation and XPRIZE Healthspan ($101M prize) push measurable rejuvenation. Together these programs form the OSK delivery foundation that Partial Reprogramming Trials will build on — the trial logistics results, the cancer screening methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as trial logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First trial logistics therapies clear regulators for specific ca
definition: 2030 milestone on the Partial Reprogramming Trials roadmap.
description:
First trial logistics therapies clear regulators for specific cancer screening conditions; trial hulls clinics open in a dozen countries.

What must be true first: the OSK delivery results have to replicate outside the lab, trial logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and cancer screening operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed OSK delivery demonstrations, trial logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting cancer screening uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Partial Reprogramming Trials
definition: Estimates Partial Reprogramming Trials readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Partial Reprogramming Trials components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a trial hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Partial Reprogramming Trials operating for a day.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where OSK delivery monitoring, trial logistics redundancy, or cancer screening maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Partial Reprogramming Trials Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Partial Reprogramming Trials: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Partial Reprogramming Trials — trials of partial cellular reprogramming.

Phase 1 — Prove (OSK delivery): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (trial logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (cancer screening): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (age reversal): trial hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and research-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
